analysis:
The only change is a documentation addition in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1745): a new row in the LaunchAgent environment passthrough table for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP. It says `0` disables the load-time shape warmup and `always` skips the shader-cache probe. It cites ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (`shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey`). The supplied base units cover only the surrounding unchanged text, and the one-line patch is complete.

The row sits in the list introduced by 'darkbloom start copies only these variables from the invoking shell into the provider plist'. That lets a reader infer the variable is forwarded to the launchd daemon, but the doc does not say so explicitly. I could not verify against the Swift source whether the key is in LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys or inferencePassthroughEnvKeys. Because that code is outside the supplied evidence, I recorded this as a possible documentation-accuracy question, not a finding.

Security relevance is low. The variable is an operator-set performance and warmup tunable, not an authentication, attestation, encryption or routing control. It does not touch the App Attest, E2E encryption, prefix-cache (T-041) or coordinator trust boundaries, and it creates no new network or privileged surface. An operator who sets it in their own environment gains nothing beyond what ADV-001 already has at the process level.

This documentation change alters no code behavior and no threat-model assumption, and I identified no regression. A later pass could confirm that the actual passthrough list contains this key and that the shader-cache probe in the warmup path does not read attacker-controlled cache data. That follow-up depends on code not supplied here.
